newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end sharply up, boosted by rate outlook.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end sharply up, boosted by rate outlook.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks rallied to a strong close on Monday as investors anticipated a steady interest rate outlook in the near term and a pick up in market tone following the Chinese New Year holiday.
The Hang Seng Index rose 129.28 points, or 0.97 percent, to 13,451.07, led by a surge in property stocks. However, turnover fell to HK$8.43 billion compared with HK$9.10 billion on Friday.
"I think most investors see interest rates staying unchanged and today you are seeing some bargain-hunting," said Henry Lui, research analyst Mansion House Research.

The U.S. Federal Reserve's policy setting body meets on Tuesday and Wednesday and analysts said recent economic data pointed to steady interest rates. U.S. data released on Friday showed a 4.7 percent rise in fourth quarter Gross Domestic Product while the GDP price index rose only 1.8 percent.
"It looks like there will be no interest increase," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities.

Analysts said the market's sluggish market tone over the last two weeks had presented a buying opportunity, particularly with some investors expecting earnings reports to boost stocks after Chinese New Year, he said.
"If Wall Street remains firm, then probably the market can test 14,000 after Chinese New Year," said Au-Young.
Property stocks led Monday's rise with Great Eagle Holdings advancing HK$1.40 to HK$32.80 following news that it plans to spin off its Tai Shan Properties unit.
Other property stocks also made strong gains, with Sun Hung Kai Properties closing at HK$90.50, up HK$3.00 and Cheung Kong rising HK$2.25 to HK$74.50.
Bank of East Asia reported a 14.5 percent rise in net profit to HK$1.88 billion on Monday but its stock ended down HK$1.00 at HK$33.90.
"If you look at the Bank of East Asia final results, I think they are pretty much what the market expected," said Lui.
But he said some investors thought the stock's valuation was too high compared with other banking stocks.
Consumer electronics products maker Chun Tai Holdings made its market debut on Monday, opening at HK$1.30 compared with an issue price of HK$1.03 and ending the session at HK$1.26.

Shares in Shui On Construction and Materials also began trading on Monday but their debut was less impressive. The stock opened at HK$9.45 compared with an issue price of HK$9.30 and closed at HK$9.05. -- Jennifer Genevieve (852) 2843 6345
